o: A person counts toward year x only while birth <= x < death — the death year itself is EXCLUDED. We return the earliest year attaining the maximum head-count. In example 2 the population is 1 during 1950-1959, rises to 2 for 1960-1969 and stays 2 through 1970-1979, then drops; the earliest peak is therefore 1960. Births and deaths all lie in [1950, 2050], so only 101 candidate years exist. Either test every year against every log (about 10^4 comparisons) or mark +1/-1 events on a timeline and prefix-sum it once; scanning years in ascending order and updating the answer only on STRICT improvement automatically yields the earliest maximizer.
k: The alive window is [birth, death - 1] — a person is not counted in their death year.
The tiny year domain (1950..2050) makes a difference array over years the natural tool.
Update the best answer with strict > so ties keep the EARLIEST year.

a.i: For every year from 1950 through 2050, count the logs satisfying birth <= year < death and track the strict maximum. With at most 100 logs and 101 years this is roughly 10^4 cheap comparisons.
s: Count people whose interval contains y as b <= y < d.
If that count strictly exceeds the best seen, record y as the answer.
a.t: O(Y*n) with Y = 101 — each of the 101 candidate years is checked against every log entry

a.i: Mark +1 at each birth year and -1 at each death year on an array indexed from 1950, then sweep once accumulating the running sum: after processing offset y the running value is exactly the population of year 1950 + y, because deaths subtract starting AT the death year. Track the strict maximum to keep the earliest peak.
s: For each log, delta[birth - 1950] += 1 and delta[death - 1950] -= 1.
Sweep offsets 0..100 adding delta[y] into a running counter.
Whenever the counter strictly exceeds the best, record 1950 + y.
a.t: O(n + Y) — one marking pass over the logs plus one sweep of the 101-year timeline

w: Either solution passes instantly; state the difference-array idea even if you code the brute force first. The recurring bug is including the death year (the condition must be year < d, never <=); the second is updating the best with >=, which returns the LATEST tied year instead of the earliest. Follow-ups: years spanning millennia (coordinate-compress the events or sort them), a stream of logs (maintain a running counter over sorted event points), or reporting the latest peak instead of the earliest.
